text:
incident-bot: Pager: Billing metering anomaly detected for tenant=acme-corp. Token count delta +21% vs expected window. Flag: potential double-count or delayed emit. Severity: P2. Runbook: /runbooks/metering -> triage.
Ryan (oncall): ack, I'm on it. Starting investigation — pulling emitter and aggregator logs.
Maya (eng-ml): noted — this lines up with a spike in our GPU batch backlog around 02:00 UTC. Could be emitter retries from backpressure.
Carla (finops): seeing a handful of overage flags firing to customers for that tenant — not widespread but visible. Do we have a count of impacted customers?
Zoe (support): customer support has 3 tickets opened for unexpected charges; all reference invoices generated around 02:15 UTC.
Ryan (oncall): quick check: `kubectl logs -n metering emitter-77 | grep "emit_success" | tail -n 50` shows intermittent retries and `HTTP 429` spikes at 02:01-02:07.
Maya (eng-ml): sending metrics link: https://dashboards.redwood.internal/metrics?panel=emitter_retries&range=3h — backpressure spike matches 02:00 UTC.
incident-bot: Note: automatic mitigation suggested -> route tenant to dedicated fallback emitter for 5m.
Ryan (oncall): manually routed acme-corp to fallback emitter group.`/api/routing/override` applied. Monitoring for duplicate emits.
Carla (finops): are we certain duplicates, or just delayed batched emits causing late counts? Difference matters for refunds.
Maya (eng-ml): preliminary: both. Some messages were retried leading to duplicate enqueue, and the aggregator's dedupe window (30s) was bypassed due to clock skew in the emitter pod.
Ryan (oncall): clock skew? Which pods? I see emitter-77 and emitter-89 with 4s drift.
Maya (eng-ml): yes — NTP sync failed during that deploy window. emitter-89 had drift ~4s, causing aggregator to treat as separate events in the current idempotency scheme.
Zoe (support): customers asking if this is billable. Any quick guidance for them?
Carla (finops): hold customer-facing comms. We should rollback manual charge flags until counts reconciled. I'll open a billing hold for acme-corp invoices between 02:00-03:00 UTC.
Ryan (oncall): mitigation notes: 1) routed tenant to fallback emitter; 2) restarted NTP on emitter nodes; 3) disabled automatic invoice emissions for affected window; 4) kicked an aggregation replay job with dedupe flag.
incident-bot: Action created: metering-6287654321 (assignee: Ryan). ETA for replay: ~12m.
Maya (eng-ml): replay job logs: `./scripts/replay.sh --tenant acme-corp --start 2026-03-17T02:00Z --end 2026-03-17T03:00Z --dedupe=true` — will report duplicates count.
Ryan (oncall): replay finished. Results: 14k emits replayed, 1.9k duplicates detected and suppressed. Net delta after suppression: +0.7% vs expected (within normal variance).
Carla (finops): good — that means most overage flags were false positives from duplicate emits. I'll clear the billing hold and mark the affected invoices for manual review (no automatic charge).
Zoe (support): updating tickets: charges reversed/under review, ETA for final confirmation 30m.
Maya (eng-ml): follow-up: we'll harden dedupe window and add additional emitter-side idempotency tokens to handle small clock drift. Filing PR for NTP alerting.
Ryan (oncall): postmortem tasks: 1) NTP monitoring alert (Maya), 2) improve emitter idempotency (Maya), 3) billing hold automation for quick rollback (Carla), 4) runbook update to include clock skew checks (Ryan).
Carla (finops): thanks — I'll prepare a short customer note template if needed.
incident-bot: Incident closed (mitigated). Root cause: emitter NTP drift causing duplicate emits under backpressure retry scenario. Severity downgraded to P3 after suppress/replay.
Ryan (oncall): closing thread. :thumbsup:
